To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nausea is triggered by 5-HT release from the interoceptive cortical insula, and is attenuated through inhibition of MAGL and activation of 5-HT1AR.
LiCl-induced 5-HT release is elevated in the IIC, is suppressed by CBD, and this is associated with suppression of nausea.
nausea-induced release of the brain neurotransmitter serotonin in the insular cortex is suppressed by the inhibition of the enzyme monoacylglycerollipase and by the administration of cannabidiol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiology of the nausea-inducing effects of the anti-psychotic, lithium chloride, in the rat.
the role that endogenous 5-HT and the endocannabinoid 2-AG, and their interactions, play in the regulation of nausea.
the role of the insular cortex in the regulation of nausea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
5-HT release is elevated in the IIC after systemic LiCl and that this release is suppressed by CBD and MAGL inhibition.
LiCl induces a nausea response that is mediated by 5-HT release from 5-HT3 terminals in the IIC.
the LiCl-induced nausea response is regulated by the release of 5-HT from the IIC, and that the release of 2-AG from the MAGL enzyme is critical to this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interoceptive IIC is a critical brain region for the mediation of nausea, where 5-HT is released in response to a nausea-inducing stimulus, and that the elevation of 5- HT in the IIC is regulated, in part, by 2-AG levels.
LiCl-induced 5-HT release is a necessary component of the conditioned response, and that this release is regulated by MAGL inhibition and CBD.
5-HT release and 5-HT3 signaling in the IIC is a key mechanism for nausea and is a target for the anti-nausea actions of CBD and MAGL inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LiCl-induced elevation in 5-HT in IIC is a key mechanism that drives the nausea response.
LiCl-induced conditioned nausea can be regulated by the release of 5-HT from the IIC and that MAGL inhibition and CBD attenuate this process by reducing 5-HT release from the IIC.
the elevation of 5HT in the insular cortex is critical for the development of nausea, and that this is regulated by the MAGL enzyme.
